orientation.summary: The 2025 North Carolina Wildlife Action Plan (SWAP) is a comprehensive state wildlife action plan from the NC Wildlife Resources Commission, submitted in 2025 as the mandatory 10-year revision of the 2015 SWAP. The document identifies Species of Greatest Conservation Need (SGCN) across all major taxonomic groups, describes natural community habitats, and outlines threats, conservation actions, and monitoring needs. The plan treats climate change as a significant and cross-cutting threat, including dedicated sections on sea level rise, temperature changes, precipitation changes, and a regional climate assessment developed in partnership with SECAS. Range shifts are addressed implicitly throughout—particularly in habitat vulnerability sections, discussions of cold-water species being displaced upslope, saltwater intrusion expanding coastal species ranges, and connectivity goals—but there are no dedicated range-shift facilitation actions. The plan incorporates prior vulnerability assessments from the NCNHP (2010, updated 2025) and references the Southeast Conservation Blueprint as a spatial prioritization tool.
